name: Japanese Kana (Hiragana and Katakana)
notes: Both syllabaries derive from man'yōgana (Chinese characters used purely phonetically for Japanese sounds, traceable to the 5th century CE); hiragana emerged as cursive simplification of whole kanji, katakana by taking fragments/components of kanji, both taking recognizable shape in the 9th-century Heian period. The popular attribution of hiragana's invention to the monk Kūkai is a legend, not documented history — no signed document supports it, and the Heian-period evidence instead shows a gradual, collective, multi-decade development with no single named inventor. Still in active use — `latest: null`.
